source.text: ወ*እምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ *መንገለ፡ ጽባሕ፡ ማእከለ፡ ለደብረ፡ መደባራ፡ ወርኢክዎ፡ ገዳመ፡ *ወባሕቲቶ፡
source.note: Fresh visual review of Charles1906 printed edition. Stars/brackets/parentheses/daggers retained where identified; not a manuscript consensus or oracle-derived source.

translation.text: From there I went east into the midst of the mountain wilderness[a], and I saw a solitary desert,

footnotes.text: The term መደባራ is a wilderness/desert term; Charles 1906 printed page 68 note 4 identifies an Aramaic loan. This clause continues into verse 2. The source is the printed Charles critical text, not the different oracle text previously placed in this record.

source.text: ምሉእ፡ ዕፀወ፡ *(ወ)እምነ፡ ዝንቱ፡ ዘርእ፡ [ወ]ማይ፡ [በላዕሉ፡] ይፈልፍል፡ እምላዕሉ፡
source.note: Fresh visual review of Charles1906 printed edition. Stars/brackets/parentheses/daggers retained where identified; not a manuscript consensus or oracle-derived source.

translation.text: full of trees. From this seed[a], water gushes from above.[b]

footnotes.text: The selected Geʿez critical text reads seed. Charles printed68 note6 treats the seed expression as problematic and considers repairs such as a mountain, plants, green growth, or sown fields. None is silently installed here.

The source brackets conjunction and above as editorially questioned material. Printed68 note7 treats the bracketed above as an interpolation. The proposed English omits those bracketed words and retains from above, which is printed without brackets.

source.text: ያስተርኢ፡ *ከመ፡ ሰረብ፡ ብዙኅ፡ [ዘይሰርብ፡] ከመ፡ መንገለ፡ መስዕ፡ መንገለ፡ ዐረብ፡ [ወ]እም፡ ኵሌሄ፡ ያዐርግ፡ †ማየ፡ ወጠለ።
source.note: Fresh visual review of Charles1906 printed edition. Stars/brackets/parentheses/daggers retained where identified; not a manuscript consensus or oracle-derived source.

translation.text: It appears like a great cloud toward the north and toward the west; from every side it raises water and dew.[a]

footnotes.text: The selected main text has †ማየ, water, marked corrupt, not the OCR form ተማየ. Charles printed68 note19 also identifies raises as an emendation with Greek assistance and proposes mist or vapour for the corrupt water expression. The bracketed rain gloss and conjunction have not been translated as unproblematic text. This provisional English follows the printed edited text without silently replacing water by mist.

source.text: ወእምህየ፡ ሖርኩ፡ መንገለ፡ መስዕ፡ በአጽናፈ፡ ምድር፡ ወበህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ምክረ፡ ዐቢየ፡ ወስብሐ፡ በአጽናፊሃ፡ ለኵላ፡ ምድር።
source.note: Fresh visual review of Charles1906 printed edition. Stars/brackets/parentheses/daggers retained where identified; not a manuscript consensus or oracle-derived source.

translation.text: From there I went north, to the ends of the earth, and there I saw a great wonder and glory[a] at the extremities of the whole earth.

footnotes.text: The printed main text reads ምክረ, with the variant መንክረ recorded in printed74 note47; it does not read OCR ምሕረ. The continuation on printed75 is ወስብሐ, and glory. The rendering is deliberately literal; great and glorious wonder is a possible smoother construction. Prior notes about a resting place or south are unsupported and must not remain attached.

source.text: ወበህየ፡ ርኢኩ፡ ኆዋኅወ፡ ሰማይ፡ ፍቱሓተ፡ በሰማይ፡ ሠለስተ፡ በበ፪*እምኔሆን፡ ይወፅኡ፡ ነፋሳት፡ በመንገለ፡ መስዕ፡ ሶበ፡ ይነፍሑ፡ ቍር፡ ወበረድ፡ ወአስኀትያ፡ ወኀመዳ፡ ወጠል፡ ወዝናም።
source.note: Fresh visual review of Charles1906 printed edition. Stars/brackets/parentheses/daggers retained where identified; not a manuscript consensus or oracle-derived source.

translation.text: There I saw three gates of heaven open in heaven. From each of them[a] north winds come out, bringing cold, hail, ice, snow, dew, and rain.[b]

footnotes.text: The exact Ethiopic numeral after በበ is not certified in this pass: OCR has ፪, while each one would require ፩. The provisional source preserves the OCR numeral pending second scan review; the English each is not yet approved.

The weather-list nouns and their fine distinctions should receive independent source-language confirmation before application. The passage is the Geʿez selected critical edition only; no surviving Greek passage was independently collated here.

source.text: ወእምአሐቲ፡ ኆኅት፡ በሠናይ፡ ይነፍኁ፡ ወሶበ፡ በአልኤሆን፡ ኆዋኅው፡ ይነፍኁ፡ †በኃይል፡ ወበጻዕር፡ ይከውን፡ ዲበ፡ ምድር፡ ወበኀይል፡ ይነፍኁ†።
source.note: Fresh visual review of Charles1906 printed edition. Stars/brackets/parentheses/daggers retained where identified; not a manuscript consensus or oracle-derived source.

translation.text: From one gate they blow favorably; but when they blow through the other gates, they blow with force, and there is distress upon the earth, and they blow strongly.[a]

footnotes.text: Charles marks the final clause with daggers as corrupt; printed75 note14 proposes a shorter reconstruction. This literal provisional English retains the repeated force/blowing clause rather than quietly adopting the conjecture. It is not certified as a reconstruction of the ancient wording.
